oos_threshold.criterion: F1 on the binary in-scope/out-of-scope decision, dev only (no intent prediction exists before the model call)

intent_descriptions.alarm_query: Requests to check or list existing alarms.
intent_descriptions.alarm_remove: Requests to cancel or delete an alarm.
intent_descriptions.alarm_set: Requests to create or schedule a new alarm.
intent_descriptions.iot_cleaning: Requests to start or stop the cleaning robot.
intent_descriptions.iot_coffee: Requests to start the coffee machine.
intent_descriptions.iot_hue_lightchange: Requests to change the colour of a light.
intent_descriptions.iot_hue_lightdim: Requests to reduce the brightness of a light.
intent_descriptions.iot_hue_lightoff: Requests to switch a light off.
intent_descriptions.iot_hue_lighton: Requests to switch a light on.
intent_descriptions.iot_hue_lightup: Requests to increase the brightness of a light.
intent_descriptions.iot_wemo_off: Requests to switch a smart plug or socket off.
intent_descriptions.iot_wemo_on: Requests to switch a smart plug or socket on.

entity_descriptions.alarm_type: Type or label of an alarm mentioned by the user.
entity_descriptions.change_amount: Amount or percentage by which a device setting should change.
entity_descriptions.color_type: Colour requested for a connected light, such as red, blue, or green.
entity_descriptions.date: Date or day mentioned for an alarm, such as tomorrow or Monday.
entity_descriptions.device_type: Household device mentioned, such as a light, cleaning robot, coffee machine, or smart plug.
entity_descriptions.general_frequency: Repetition frequency explicitly mentioned for an alarm, such as daily or every weekday.
entity_descriptions.house_place: Room or location inside the home, such as bedroom, kitchen, or living room.
entity_descriptions.time: Specific clock time mentioned for an alarm, such as 6 AM or 8:30 PM.
entity_descriptions.timeofday: Part of the day mentioned for an alarm, such as morning or evening.

effort.note: active human minutes are self-reported and exclude breaks and model waiting time. Wall clock is elapsed time since `start`, which includes both.

ai_assistance: used the internet and Claude's explanation of the configuration options and terms (plus the scripts/b2_examples.py example viewer) to understand them; chose the configuration and wrote all descriptions myself
notes: I selected twostage-sim-tfidf because the two-stage approach first identifies the user's intent and then extracts the required information. Similarity-based examples help the model understand different ways of expressing commands. TF-IDF helps reject requests outside the supported tasks. A possible disadvantage is that the two-stage approach requires two model calls, which may increase response time. TF-IDF may also reject some valid requests with unusual wording.
bias_note: the same person built the automated system and this manual baseline, and already knows the data. This is a single, non-blind measurement of setup effort and must be reported as such.
